## Summary

The April 22, 2026 overview describes an embeddable UI for collecting complete shipping and billing addresses in an app, including full billing addresses for uses such as tax. The November 7, 2026 parent page links to iOS, Android and React Native overview variants. The separate [[source-stripe-inapp-collect-addresses|Collect addresses implementation guide]] provides April implementation details. Its November parent page has four links because it splits iOS into UIKit and SwiftUI.

## April 2026 Features

- **236 regional address formats**, including right-to-left formats.
- **Autocomplete.** The overview describes built-in suggestions. The implementation guide says iOS enables autocomplete by default. Android, including React Native on Android, requires the Google Places SDK and API key to enable suggestions. The captures give no measured conversion improvement.
- **Saved-address prefill.** An address can be prefilled when it is already saved for the customer.
- **Appearance API.** Configure the component’s appearance to match the integration.
- **Availability.** The April overview lists availability for web, iOS, Android and React Native SDKs. The April iOS overview describes reusing an existing Elements instance and automatically passing address data with Payment Sheet and Payment Element. The April Android and React Native overviews describe Elements reuse and automatic data passing with Payment Element and Link.

## Address data in mobile and web integrations

In the April mobile implementation guide, the documented iOS UIKit and Android examples optionally pass the collected address as `PaymentSheet.Configuration.shippingDetails`. React Native uses `defaultShippingDetails`. When populated, the payment UI prefills billing and shows an option to use the shipping address for billing. The guide documents `PaymentIntent.shipping` when the intent is confirmed with the configured details. Completing the mobile address UI or prefilling fields does not confirm payment or automatically persist an address server-side.

The separate [[source-stripe-address-element|web Address Element]] guide documents routing address and payment data on confirmation when the components share a Stripe.js Elements instance. See [[stripe-address-element]] for that web route.

payments-mobile-address-element.text: Use the Address Element to collect complete billing and shipping addresses for in-app integrations.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:
- **Global support**: Support 236 regional address formats, including right-to-left address formats

- **Seamless Elements integration**: Reuse an existing Elements instance to save time, and pass data automatically with the [Payment Sheet](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-sheet.md) and [Payment Element](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/embedded.md)
- **Seamless Elements integration**: Reuse an existing Elements instance to save time, and pass data automatically with the Payment Element and Link

payments-mobile-address-element.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/address-element, the November 7 capture describes an Address Element for complete in-app billing and shipping addresses and links the iOS, Android and React Native variants. It contains no per-platform setup or payment flow (new raw lines 5-15). The April 22 capture describes the embeddable UI and full billing use such as tax. All three expanded overviews list 236 regional address formats including right-to-left, autocomplete, prefill if a customer address is already saved, Appearance API customization, and web/mobile availability. The listed integration and data-passing partners are iOS Payment Sheet and Payment Element, and Android and React Native Payment Element and Link (old raw lines 8-26, old raw lines 28-46, old raw lines 48-66). The candidate for source-stripe-inapp-address-element.md preserves the April component and common features, scopes the named pairings to the captured platforms, and links the existing Collect addresses guide. Collecting or prefilling an address is UI state; the distinct implementation guide documents optional shipping-details configuration and PaymentIntent.shipping on confirmation with those details populated (raw/stripe-inapp-collect-addresses-2025.md:136-148,524-532,711-717).
payments-mobile-address-element.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/address-element, the capture changes are navigation and presentation. November indexes the three mobile variants and no longer embeds their April bodies, screenshots or Collect addresses links. It supplies no product-level change or withdrawal evidence. Keep the April feature list, 236 formats including RTL, saved-address prerequisite for prefill, Appearance API, named integration pairs, and guide routes dated in source-stripe-inapp-address-element.md (old raw lines 8-26, old raw lines 28-66, new raw lines 5-15). Correct the stale guide status and link this overview and source-stripe-inapp-collect-addresses.md in both directions through the in-app concept. The companion’s separately captured November index lists iOS UIKit, iOS SwiftUI, Android and React Native. This overview lists three platform links. Keep the companion’s detailed implementation dated to April (raw/stripe-payments-mobile-collect-addresses-2026-11-07.md:5-16, wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-collect-addresses.md:11-24,128-136). The April companion guide documents optional passing of the collected shipping address through PaymentSheet.Configuration.shippingDetails on iOS and Android and defaultShippingDetails on React Native. These settings prefill billing and display the option to reuse the shipping address as billing. With the configured details populated, PaymentIntent.shipping is documented when the intent is confirmed (raw/stripe-inapp-collect-addresses-2025.md:136-148,524-532,711-717). The separate web route combines address and payment data on confirmation when the components share the same Stripe.js Elements instance (wiki/concepts/stripe-address-element.md:27-41). iOS autocomplete is on by default. Android autocomplete, including React Native on Android, requires the Google Places SDK and an API key (raw/stripe-inapp-collect-addresses-2025.md:12-18,457-469,644-656). Collection or a UI callback does not establish payment success or an automatic server update, and the November overview establishes no SDK or REST API version, payment outcome, or measured conversion improvement.
